**Test image observations:**
- Close-up of a green soybean stem at a node
- Dark brown/black discoloration concentrated at the node area
- Small dark specks/structures visible on the stem surface

**Comparison with references:**
- **Diaporthe** (upper-right reference): Shows very similar dark discoloration at nodes on green stems with black pycnidia - strong match. The KB describes "black, raised specks (pycnidia) appearing in linear rows on mature soybean stems" and "small black specks form on stems, petioles, pods at nodes."
- **Phytophthora** (bottom-right reference): Similar node discoloration but typically extends from the soil line upward as a chocolate-brown lesion.
- **White_Mold**: Characterized by fluffy white mycelial growth, not seen here.
- **Anthracnose**: Shows lesions more on pods/mature tissue.
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Internal microsclerotia, different presentation.
- **Phomopsis**: Primarily affects pods/seeds.

The dark specks on the stem surface at and around the node, combined with the overall pattern of discoloration on a still-green stem, best matches Diaporthe (pod and stem blight). The linear arrangement of black pycnidia on stems is the distinguishing diagnostic feature.
